answer:
Use legacy FEniCS/dolfin and solve a 2D plane-strain quasi-incompressible finite-strain neo-Hookean problem with mixed displacement-pressure unknowns u and p.
Create a mesh of the rectangle (0,1.0)x(0,0.20) with circular holes of radius 0.04 centered at (0.40,0.10) and (0.60,0.10).
Use E=5 MPa and ν=0.49.
Use a stable mixed finite element pair, for example Taylor-Hood P2/P1.
Define F=I+grad u, C=F^T F, and J=det(F).
Use the quasi-incompressible neo-Hookean mixed energy W(u,p)=μ/2(tr(C)-2-2ln J)+p(J-1)-p^2/(2κ), with μ=E/(2(1+ν)) and κ=E/(3(1-2ν)).
Fix the left edge x=0 with u_x=0 and u_y=0.
Prescribe the right edge x=1.0 with u_x=0.060 m and u_y=0.
Leave the top and bottom edges traction-free.
Apply a uniform compressive hole pressure P_hole=0.10 MPa on each hole boundary.
For the hole pressure load, use the outward unit normals of the undeformed hole boundaries, not the current deformed normals, and integrate the traction -P_hole N over the reference hole boundaries.
Solve the resulting nonlinear mixed problem with Newton's method.
After convergence, compute the Cauchy stress from the displacement and pressure fields.
Compute the von Mises stress from the deviatoric part of the Cauchy stress.
Save a colour map of the pressure p as q14_p.png.
Save a colour map of the von Mises stress as q14_vm.png.
Save the displacement field in XDMF format.
